title_en: Holy Company with the Saint at Shahpura
translation:
Nana Gopaldas and other devotees came from Malwa together with Jivanji Maharaj and settled at the station of Shahpura. This Nana Gopaldas was from Chanderiya. He was inquisitive by nature, and so he used to hold very extensive discussions on dharma with Jivanji Maharaj. And whatever Jivanji Maharaj told him, Haridas would write down — these words and teachings of Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj. That writing exists with us to this day. We call it the Samagam (the Holy Discourse) of Jivanji Maharaj.

(Based on the couplets of Jivanji Maharaj!)

When Jivanji Maharaj went from near Vadsar to an ochhav (festive gathering) at Samiyala, he took Gopaldas Haribhai from Dhanyavi along with him. Haribhai was so overcome with longing for the darshan of the Guru that, while walking along the road, he began reciting a couplet, saying:

_Kabir nadiya jal koyla bhai, samudra laagi aag ||_
_Machhi ja tarvar chadhi, uth Kabira jaag ||1||_
("Kabir says: the water of the rivers has turned to charcoal, and fire has broken out in the ocean; the fish has climbed up into a tree — arise, O Kabir, awake!" — "The river of my hope and craving has burned to ashes, and a fire has broken out in the ocean of my worldly desire. So the fish of my own mind, to escape the fire of illusion (maya), taking refuge in me, has climbed up onto the tree that is the guru who can ferry me across the ocean of birth and death. That is to say, I have become frantic to meet the Guru.")

Seeing Haribhai in such a state, the merciful Lord Jivanji Maharaj at once spoke this couplet:

_Kabir muj virahankun piu muyu, dagh diyo nav jaay ||_
_Maans gali gali bhuy pade, aur kanak rahi galelaay ||2||_
("Just as a widow, scorched by the unbearable fire of separation from her husband, has her flesh fall away in charred lumps upon the ground, and yet lives on by the barest support of the little that clings on like a fleck of gold — such was my own anguish too, for meeting a lover like you.")

So Jivanji Maharaj, granting this loving Haridas the garland and the tilak, took him into his refuge.

There are, in this way, four Gopaldas: Nana Gopaldas of Chanderiya, Mota Gopaldas of Khediya, Sant Gopaldas of Shahpura, and Guru Gopaldas (according to the Samagam). Of these, Mota Gopaldas of Khediya arranged the darshan of Jivanji Maharaj for the Gopaldas of Chanderiya. Nana Gopaldas had been eager for a guru, and had told Mota Gopaldas of Khediya, "If any saint should come, do arrange a meeting for me." So Mota Gopaldas brought that Nana Gopaldas of Chanderiya along to have darshan of Jivanji Maharaj. This Nana Gopaldas was extremely inquisitive, and having had darshan of Jivanji Maharaj he was deeply moved, and in a couplet of offering he says:

_Chanderie vaase vasu, Jivan pragate aay_
_Sitapati Raghunathko, dino naam bataay_
("I dwell residing in Chanderiya; there Jivanji Maharaj appeared and came, and he gave and showed me the name of Raghunath, the Lord of Sita.")

This inquisitive devotee used to have many discussions with Jivanji Maharaj, and Haridas of Nadiad wrote down those discussions, along with the couplets that Jivanji Maharaj must have spoken, in the book of the Samagam. Thus this Haridas of Nadiad has done our community a very great service. Had he not written anything at all, we would have been left deprived of the Guru's own words.
